prose: In the 1987 election to the 140-seat Kerala Legislative Assembly, the Left Democratic Front (LDF) emerged largest with 78 seats, against 61 for the UDF (1 to others/independents). Turnout was 80.55% of 15,948,137 electors.
By vote share, the LDF polled 44.97% and the UDF 43.55%, with the NDA on 6.48%. A total of 628 candidates contested the 140 seats.
Compared with 1982, the LDF gained 15 seats (from 63 to 78); the UDF moved from 77 to 61. Power changed hands from the UDF.
The closest contest was Hosdurg, won by N. Manoharan Master (Cong-I) over Pallipram Balan (CPI) by just 59 votes. The largest margin was E. Ahamed in Tanur (35,785 votes).
E.K. Nayanar headed the Council of Ministers that followed.
